title: Conditional formatting ods 002
notes: real ODF 1.2 conditional formats (ODF 1.2 §9.4, the LO 4.x on-disk shape that replaced the ODF 1.1 style:map workaround): two table:conditional-formats: one over Mixed.A1:A3 with TWO table:conditions — numeric "this-cell() >= 50" -> GP Warn (#FFEB9C) and text test "contains(this-cell(); \"urgent\")" -> GP Bad — and one over the date column Mixed.C1:C3 with the date condition string "this-cell() > DATE(2026;1;1)" -> GP Warn; column C holds real date cells (office:value-type="date"). table:conditional-format sits under office:spreadsheet after the table element; conditions are table:condition elements with table:test (OpenFormula with this-cell(), semicolon argument separator), table:apply-style and table:base-cell-address. LO-tolerance items NOT verified here (LibreOffice is not run in this environment, so they are recorded, not claimed): (a) table:apply-style pointing at a NAMED style — LO's own writer usually emits automatic styles there, named-style references are valid style-name references but LO round-trip tolerance is unverified; (b) address qualification — target-range-address is table-qualified (Numbers.A1:Numbers.A10) while base-cell-address is unqualified (A1), matching LO's on-disk form as best known; (c) whether the conditional-format element must sit after vs before the tables — emitted after; (d) LO evaluation of the exact this-cell()/contains()/DATE() test strings at render time. Reference text is the plain stored cell strings (condition colors are display-time, never text); the normative counter reads table:table=1.
